title: Native patch: handling file permission properly

timeline.message:
Native patch: handling file permission properly

1. If no file permission is specified in the patch file, preserve the
original file permission.

2. If file permission is specified, then set it as it is.

Fixes https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/10913

RELNOTES: Native patch can handle file permission properly
timeline.author: Yun Peng

We can use bit-operators here to test for the bits in the permission bitmask :)

Executable is `0b001 = 1`
Writable is `0b010 = 2`
Readable is `0b100 = 4`

So we can replace this with:

```java
return permission & 4;
```

reply.body: So this test case is for testing an error message is thrown when no input and output file name is specified. Before, we only parse file names from `---` and `+++` lines. But now we also parses file names from `diff --git` line, therefore we should also remove them here to keep the test passing.

timeline.body:
If you want to use some more exotic Java data types, you could use `Optional<BitSet>` for the filePermission type (and `BitSet` in general, rather than an `int`, to store the permissions). Then you could use an `enum` as the keys for the `BitSet` (e.g. `EXECUTABLE = 0, WRITABLE = 1, READABLE = 2`).

But using `-1` as the indicator for "no explicit permissions" is also fine, if you prefer it. ;)

reply.body: I tried to use BitSet, but found converting a character (eg. `7`) to a BitSet also requires some steps. The code overall didn't look much cleaner, so I'll keep using `-1` and bit operations ;)
